items.title: Wall St futures extend gains after economic data
items.summary:
US stock index futures moved higher on Wednesday as a cooler-than-anticipated inflation reading lifted hopes that the Federal Reserve might not raise interest rates as soon as next month.

items.title: Inflation cooled slightly last month even as consumers stepped up spending
items.summary: U.S. markets bounced higher immediately on the new inflation reading, with investors betting that an expected interest-rate hike from the U.S. Federal Reserve might be delayed.

items.title: Ruddy: Trump's Real Enemy Is the Federal Reserve
items.summary: Newsmax CEO Christopher Ruddy argues that the Federal Reserve, rather than the media, poses the greater threat to President Donald Trump and Republicans by keeping interest rates elevated despite what he describes as largely supply-driven inflation, increasing economic pressure ahead of the midterms.

items.title: Ringgit ends slightly higher against Greenback on Fed rate outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 (Bernama) -- The ringgit ended slightly higher against the greenback on Wednesday, supported by expectations that the US Federal Reserve (Fed) may hold off on raising interest rates next month following weaker-than-expected consumer sentiment data.

items.title: Gold on track for monthly decline as investors brace for US inflation data
items.summary: Gold prices steadied ​on Wednesday but were headed for a monthly loss as expectations of higher interest ‌rates weighed on sentiment, while investors awaited US inflation data for clues on the Federal Reserve's next policy move.

items.title: Gold heads for monthly decline, US inflation data looms
items.summary: On Wednesday, gold prices remained stable, although they are poised for a monthly decline. Market participants are scrutinizing US inflation metrics to gauge the Federal Reserve's upcoming policies. The anticipated rise in interest rates is impacting gold alongside other precious metals. Additionally, a significant drop in consumer confidence has emerged amid worries over economic stability and tensions in the Middle East.

items.title: Fed's Williams sees no urgency for next rate hike
items.summary: Federal Reserve policymakers probably only need to deliver one more rate hike this year to get inflation back on track to the US central bank's 2 per cent goal, says New York Fed President John Williams.

items.title: US Federal Reserve’s Williams sees one more interest rate hike in late 2026
items.summary: But he said there was no urgency to act following the Fed's decision to lift rates this month. Read more at straitstimes.com.

items.title: Fed rate hike 'not urgent', says John Williams; Austan Goolsbee warns against 'playing with fire'
items.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams stated there could be one more interest rate increase before year-end. He emphasized that the central bank is not in a hurry to act immediately as it awaits more economic data. Williams projected that inflation might end the year at approximately 3.5% before returning to the Fed's target by 2028.

items.title: Euro Falls to 16-Month Low as Hawkish Fed Bets Boost Dollar
items.summary: The euro fell to its weakest level in 16 months as expectations that the Federal Reserve will further boost interest rates supported the US dollar.
